name: Independent Interrogative Genitive Pronoun NP

1.definition: Interrogative independent genitive pronoun functioning as an NP

projection.target: Whose can occur as a clause-level complement in Whose is this? and as an interrogative fused head in Whose did you borrow? The dependent use in Whose key is this? includes a separate nominal.
projection.evidence: CGEL distinguishes three slots for whose and gives an independent NP use with nominal interpretation recovered from context.

curious.title: Asking whose it is
curious.summary: The word whose can stand alone as a question about the owner of something.
curious.body:
In Whose is this?, the word whose asks who the owner is, and it stands alone with no noun after it. We can leave the noun out because the situation shows what we're talking about.

Whose can also show up in other places. In Whose did you borrow?, it again stands for the thing and its owner together. In Whose key is this?, a noun follows it, so that's a different pattern.
curious.try: Hold up something that belongs to someone else and ask whose it is. Do you need to say what it is?

teacher.summary: Covers whose used as a freestanding NP in a question, and how it differs from whose before a noun.
teacher.explain: The independent interrogative genitive pronoun is a form of whose that functions as an NP with no following noun. It asks for the possessor, as in Whose is this? The dictionary distinguishes three slots for whose: a clause-level complement (Whose is this?), an interrogative fused head (Whose did you borrow?), and a dependent use with a separate nominal (Whose key is this?). In the independent use, the nominal interpretation is recovered from context. The dictionary marks this account as provisional.
teacher.terms: Whose is sometimes called an interrogative possessive. This grammar says genitive instead of possessive.
watch_for: A learner might think whose must be followed by a noun.
A learner might read the whose of Whose did you borrow? as asking about a person, when it asks about the owner of the thing borrowed.
teacher.activity: Collect a few items from the class. Students ask each other whose each one is, once with a noun and once without, and note where the noun can be left out.

child.hook: Which tiny word asks who owns something?
child.explain: The word whose asks who owns something. You can use it alone. You might hold up a jacket and ask, "Whose is this?"
child.play: Collect three things from around the room. Ask "Whose is this?" for each one, and see who can answer.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Independent Interrogative Genitive Pronoun NP." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/np-pron-interrog-gen-indep-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
